work_item: Harden the manual Canon MCP production deployment after Cloudflare authentication/account routing failures.

observed_failures.finding: Manual deployment reached Wrangler with no CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN or account ID configured and failed before deployment.

Later deployment had Cloudflare credentials present but failed at /accounts/<configured>/workers/services/canon-read-only-mcp with Cloudflare error 7003, consistent with a stale or inaccessible configured account identifier.

root_cause: The workflow forced CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID from a repository secret. Wrangler treats that static value as authoritative before its own API-backed account selection, so a stale account ID prevented recovery.
remediation: Provide CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN to Wrangler but omit the stale static account ID.
Run wrangler whoami --json before deployment to fail early when authentication is invalid.
Allow Wrangler to fetch accessible accounts and auto-select when exactly one account is available; non-interactive ambiguous account selection remains fail-closed.
Add a regression test preventing CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID from being reintroduced into the deployment workflow.
